name: Sheet-Pan Bratwurst with Peppers and Potatoes
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified 512 cal / 22g protein at the source, so calories clear and protein needs only a small bump. Second bratwurst dish and the only sheet-pan entry with peppers, which keeps it distinct from the cabbage-and-potato skillet. All ingredients board-tracked. Sheet-pan roasting is the single easiest format to double for 14 servings. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Everything hits one sheet pan and the oven does the rest. Bratwurst roasted over potatoes, sweet peppers, onions and a real pile of mushrooms, all of it browning together while you do something else. It is a hearty plate at {{protein}} grams of protein, and it runs about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Chicken Broth, 2.5 cups: ~$0.96. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Pantry seasonings (dried thyme, black pepper, salt): ~$0.80. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $49.75 across 14 servings, so roughly $3.55 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $52.88 across 14 servings, roughly $3.78 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $10.89 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $63.77. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). The mushrooms and red peppers push it up, so read the shopping tips below before you commit.
shop_smart: The mushrooms and red peppers are the whole story. Together they are more than half the batch cost. Cut either one in half and this recipe drops into normal territory fast.
Green peppers instead of red saves real money. Red peppers are just ripened green ones and they carry a hefty premium for it. Roasting sweetens either color.
Watch for the sliced mushroom packs on markdown. Mushrooms hit the discount rack constantly because they bruise. They roast down to nothing here, so cosmetic flaws do not matter.
Brats on sale are the move. Buy the five packs when the price drops and freeze them. They thaw in the fridge overnight with no loss.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F and get two or three large sheet pans out. Crowding is the enemy of browning, so use more pans than you think you need.
Cut the potatoes into small chunks, slice the onions and red peppers thick, quarter the mushrooms and mince the garlic.
Toss the potatoes with olive oil, dried thyme, salt and black pepper, spread them out, and give them a head start in the oven since they take the longest.
Add the onions, peppers, mushrooms and garlic to the pans and toss everything together with the potatoes.
Lay the bratwurst on top of the vegetables so they roast in the open air and get color on the skin.
Roast until the brats are browned and cooked through and the vegetables have caught at the edges, turning the pans once partway.
Splash the chicken broth onto the hot pans to lift the browned bits, then combine everything with those juices in your big pot.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, slicing the brats first so the meat spreads evenly. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Toss the potato chunks with olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper and give them a head start at 425F.
Add the sliced onions, peppers, quartered mushrooms and garlic to the pans and toss together.
Lay the bratwurst on top of the vegetables.
Roast until the brats brown and the vegetables catch at the edges, turning the pans once.
Deglaze the hot pans with chicken broth and combine everything with the juices.
